chapter: Records, Lovie Austin and a first marriage
title: Lovie Austin's kindness and the origin of "Down Hearted Blues"
summary: Hunter recounts humming the tune and verses to Lovie, who thought it a good song and offered to record it; she gave Lovie the tune and kept the words.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I was going to ask -- before we go on, I was going to ask you about people like Lovie. Now, I met Lovie, as you know --
-- yeah, in 1961. And -- but what was Lovie like back then in the old days at Paramount?

Lovie was a wonderful woman. She was kind hearted. She tried to help anybody and everybody that she could. You know, because now, for instance, when I wrote 'Down Hearted Blues', when I came up from Memphis with the little 'Down Hearted Blues' in my young heart, you know, why when I hummed this thing to her, and she said, ooh, that's pretty, she said, so she -- and then I sang the verse to her, that verse that I said, 'the sun shining high goin' shine in my door some day, because good luck is a fortune, and it's bound to fall my way', she said, o-oh, that's wonderful, honey, she said.

And I kept singing the different little verses, and I -- as I would -- as I was singing, different little things would come to me that rhymed, and I would let it go like this verse. She said, oh, that's wonderful. She kept saying that.

So eventually, why, she said, that's a good song. That'll make a good song. So I, not knowing anything about copyrights and things like that, so I said, you think so? So she said yes. So she said -- she had been recording with other people, so she said, oh, maybe we can make a record of that. So, I said, me, I can't make no records.

She said, oh, yes, you can. So I said, I tell you all right then, if you think it could be a good song, why, you can have the tune that I'm humming, and I'll take the words that I'm singing. So she said, oh, yeah? I said, yes, you can have the tune. So she sent it to Washington, had it copywritten and had it copywritten in my name, to show you what an honest woman she was, because she could have stolen the whole thing from me, and I would never have known the difference.
